summary:
ASTRA is an astronaut health-monitoring and wellness-support prototype designed to support the physical and mental well-being of astronauts during space missions. It combines vital-sign monitoring, daily health routines, mood tracking, and health trends in one interactive application.

Astronauts face unique challenges in space, including fluid redistribution in microgravity, disrupted sleep cycles, physical deconditioning, and psychological stress. ASTRA addresses these challenges by allowing users to record vital signs such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, body temperature, and respiratory rate, while also tracking hydration, exercise, nutrition, sleep, and mental well-being.

By bringing health measurements and daily wellness activities together, ASTRA aims to make health information easier to understand and encourage consistent self-monitoring. The project explores how digital technology and NASA's human-spaceflight research can support healthier, more informed space missions.
details:
ASTRA is an astronaut health-monitoring and wellness-support system developed to help astronauts monitor their physical health and maintain healthy daily routines during space missions.

The application is built using a Flask-based Python backend and an interactive web interface. It consists of several interconnected modules, including a Dashboard, Daily Care, Health Monitoring, Alerts, and Trends.

The Daily Care module helps users keep track of hydration, exercise, nutrition, sleep, and mental well-being. The Health Monitoring module allows users to record vital signs, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, body temperature, respiratory rate, and sleep duration. An assessment engine processes recorded measurements and provides health-status indicators and alerts. The Trends module allows users to review historical health records and observe changes over time.

Technology and development: ASTRA uses Python and Flask for backend development, SQLite for database management, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for frontend development and interactive functionality. The application stores health records in an SQLite database, allowing information to persist between sessions.

Innovation and impact: ASTRA combines health monitoring, preventive wellness routines, alerts, and historical data analysis in one platform. Rather than simply displaying health measurements, it aims to help astronauts understand their health patterns and become more aware of potential concerns.

The project considers the unique challenges of spaceflight, including microgravity-related fluid redistribution, disrupted sleep cycles, physical deconditioning, and psychological well-being. NASA's published human-spaceflight research informed its design and wellness recommendations.

ASTRA is currently a prototype and does not connect to live spacecraft telemetry or replace professional medical assessment.
